robot: MyoHand on a positioned forearm (MyoDex, MyoSuite, MuJoCo): 39 hand muscles plus 6 position servos that place the forearm

frame.base_text: the simulator's world frame (z up): camera poses are given in it; no part here takes an end-effector pose

arm.note: the forearm's placement servos: position targets of joints ARTx, ARTy, ARTz (sliding, m; ranges [-0.75, 0.5], [-0.5, 0.5], [-0.5, 0.3]) and ARRx, ARRy, ARRz (rotations, rad, [-1.75, 1.75]); the hand's 39 muscles are columns 6-44 of action type actuators

resets.note: Each episode starts from the same frozen state; only the last episode is graded, and a success ends the run at once.

notes: A muscle's command a sets its excitation u = 1 / (1 + exp(-5 (a - 0.5))), not clipped (a = -1: about 0.0006, a = 0.5: 0.5, a = 1: 0.92); activation follows excitation with a short delay (about 10 ms up, 40 ms down); muscles only pull, one muscle can cross several joints, and its force depends on its length and speed. Before your first command of an episode every column holds -1 (all muscles relaxed). Action type actuators has 45 columns: 0-5 are the forearm's position servos (the part arm: move_robot / execute_trajectory space joint keep the muscles at their last command), 6-44 the hand's 39 muscles, which you command with execute_trajectory space native (action_type actuators). The robot's own action type takes one row per control step (0.01 s, 100 Hz), columns in its layout (describe_robot: action_types_native; spec_file has each actuator, muscle and joint). The state is proprio_now (layout in spec_file: proprio_layout, proprio_groups): joint positions and velocities, muscle activations and lengths, joint efforts. There is no joint-level controller: joints move only through muscle forces. Time passes only inside calls; the service says when the episode ended and why, never the object or goal state.
